chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Fajr, and when he finished, he turned his face towards his companions and asked about some people, 'Did they attend?' They said, 'No, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'Are they absent?' They said, 'No.' He said, 'Indeed, there is no prayer more difficult for the hypocrites than this prayer and the Isha prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Why are Fajr and Isha prayers considered most difficult for hypocrites?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize the spiritual rigor required of the faithful, contrasting the ease of prayer for believers with the burden it places on hypocrites (al-munafiqun) who struggle to maintain consistency. The Prophet’s specific inquiry into the absence of certain individuals highlights the communal nature of worship, where regular attendance in congregation is a key marker of sincerity. This hadith underscores the unique difficulty of the Fajr and Isha prayers, which are often cited in Shia jurisprudence as times when the lazy or insincere are most likely to falter.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. al-Hassan b. Ali al-Washa from Abdillah b. Sinan from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:
“Didn’t they come? Remember it that offering of no other Salaat is difficult for a hypocrite except this and Isha Salaat.”
